scenario.title: Connections and background runtime lifecycle
situations: A user changes the selected Yoke connection or loses access to its server.
The local core, local PostgreSQL, relay or dashboard is stopped or stale.
Logging out or shutting down a machine interrupts background work.
An operator maintains a self-hosted server after initial setup.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Verify core build/start/upgrade audience rather than inferring it from a command namespace.
Trace self-host sign-in, service upgrade/teardown and auth removal without treating them as everyday first-use steps.

lessons.title: Separate connection, universe and application environment
lessons.when: When switching, repairing or removing a Yoke connection.
lessons.need: Know which control plane the CLI is addressing and whether an action only changes this client or changes shared state; do not confuse that connection with an application deployment target.
lessons.surface: config/status, env, auth, connect/connection; HTTPS diagnostics
lessons.gap: Mode selection is mapped, but ongoing connection lifecycle is not yet traced. Review question: should connection errors and switching help explain the affected machine/universe before recommending repair?

lessons.title: Name the component that must be running
lessons.when: When work fails because core/database/relay/UI service is down or a session ends.
lessons.need: Read the component status, ownership, version and supported restart/resume procedure; distinguish host login lifetime from server reachability.
lessons.surface: core/local-postgres/relay/ui/self-host operation families; Linux supervision guidance
lessons.gap: Runtime control commands are exposed, but this census does not decide which are ordinary product operations versus source-development tools. Review question: should existing status/help docs provide a small component-to-recovery map?
